author: Reference cases from the implementation report §12.3 plus cases derived by exact rational arithmetic in tests/reference/oracles/quadratic.ts, which shares no code with the catalogue kernel.
review: No independent human subject reviewer has approved these cases. Automated agreement is engineering evidence only.
semantics: f(x) = a·x²/2 with a > 0; x[n+1] = (1 − p)·x[n] where p = η·a is the IEEE-754 double product of the inputs, computed once. Positions, gradients a·x[n] and losses a·x[n]²/2 are exact values for those inputs, rounded once to the nearest double. The regime depends only on (x0, p): zero-start if x0 = 0, else stationary (p = 0), monotone-convergence (0 < p < 1), one-step (p = 1), alternating-convergence (1 < p < 2), oscillation (p = 2), divergence (p > 2).
format: Arrays align with indices. A number is expected for valid statuses and null for numerical limits. Status "valid:UNDERFLOW" is a valid subnormal value carrying an UNDERFLOW approximation; "numerical-limit:OVERFLOW" means the exact magnitude exceeds Number.MAX_VALUE; "numerical-limit:UNDERFLOW" means a nonzero exact value rounds to zero. lastFiniteIndex is the last iteration before the first overflow of that quantity. An observed number o matches expected e when |o − e| <= absolute + relative·|e|; tolerance 0 is used only when every expected position, loss and gradient is exactly representable. Regimes, statuses and lastFiniteIndex always match exactly.
